title.narrative: Initiative for Rural Rehabilitation in Syria - ILRS III

description.narrative:
Context:
The impact of the protracted conflict in Syria on an already fragile sector, compounded by consecutive droughts has reduced access to irrigation water and electricity. As a result, options for sustainable livelihood development have been markedly reduced, and traditional social safety nets wiped out. The rising number of female-led households and individuals with disabilities are especially vulnerable. Syrias food production has hit an all-time low, as cultivable areas have shrunk due to shortages and rising costs of inputs. Roughly 50% of farmers have minimal or no access to essential inputs. Erratic rainfall patterns, droughts, and floods have elevated the risk of seasonal crop failures, reduced yields, and contributed to soil erosion. Furthermore, the existing agricultural workforce is inadequately equipped to adapt to these climate change-induced challenges that are specific to their region. Current agricultural practices, including flood irrigation, over-extraction of groundwater, and overgrazing by livestock, are unsustainable and could lead to the total collapse of the sector. All these factors combined have serious consequences for agribusiness and food security, and subsequently for household and private sector incomes. They are also a major driver of localized conflicts, as communities compete for access to farmable lands or groundwater. The conflict has directly damaged agricultural infrastructure, rendering the few state institutions non-functional due to insufficient staff and funds. The agricultural extension service, which encompassed veterinary services and kept track of local production, was discontinued following the Syrian states withdrawal. Employment and training are scarce and trade in locally produced food is hindered by the country?s political fragmentation and limited access to markets. This fragmentation also obstructs the development of national strategies for water and agriculture, which are essential for addressing underlying issues and enhancing communities ability to handle future challenges. As a result, the resilience of local agricultural and food systems to external shocks is inadequate.
Objective:
The program aims to strengthen the resilience of agricultural and food systems in Northern Syria.
Approach:
It focuses on enhancing the capabilities of local target groups and MSMEs in agricultural value chains, along with implementing measures for natural resource protection, early warning systems, and environmental and climate risk management strategies for communities and the private sector. At the same time, the program targets the immediate needs caused by secondary and tertiary impacts of the protracted crisis such as economic volatility, lack of basic services and collapse of state structures. The intervention will be implemented through the promotion of alternative and sustainable practices and technologies by farmers, pastoralists, agricultural cooperatives and MSMEs along high-potential value chains and private services. Strengthening the capacities of target groups to adapt to climate change will be a key element of the funding strategy. By addressing the linkages between agriculture, livelihoods and climate/environment, the project promotes the resilience of local agricultural and food systems. The program focuses on five main fields of action in which integrative and sustainable approaches to strengthening resilience at municipal level are applied: 1. improving integrated food security 2. improving and expanding access to agricultural water resources, including reclaimed wastewater 3. municipal environmental restoration and protection 4. mitigating the socio-economic and health impacts of the COVID-19 pandemic 5. improving the access of agricultural MSMEs to markets and business services
Die Resilienz der lokalen Agrar- und Ernährungssysteme in Nordsyrien ist systemisch gestärkt.

condition.narrative: Conditions - Technical Cooperation is provided free of charge to the partner country; onlending by the partner country government to the project-executing agency as a loan (splitting of terms) is generally not foreseen. Financially strong partner countries are to contribute visibly more to the costs of the development measures in accordance with their capacity.

Konditionen - Die TZ erfolgt gegenüber dem Partnerland unentgeltlich; eine Weiterleitung durch die Regierung des Partnerlandes an den Projektträger als Darlehen (Konditionenspaltung) wird grundsätzlich nicht vorgenommen. Finanzstarke Partnerländer sollen sich entsprechend ihrer Leistungsfähigkeit sichtbar stärker an den Kosten der Entwicklungsmaßnahmen beteiligen
